extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in wartime reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary newspaper reporting of battlefield developments, combining dispatches, official communiqués, radio-recorded broadcasts and correspondent eye-witness accounts to inform a general public about military operations. Emphasizes datelines, source attribution, geographic/numeric detail and human-interest color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and byline
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a location and date dateline and reporter credit (e.g., 'Kairouan, Tunisia, April 13—', 'By DEWITT MACKENZIE', '—By WILLIAM B. KING').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear datelines and bylines so readers know where and when the dispatch originated and who filed it; the page shows multiple datelines and bylines for different dispatches and features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution for reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute information to its originating source, especially broadcasts and foreign radio (e.g., '(The Algiers radio, in a broadcast recorded in London, said...)', 'The German radio said today in a broadcast recorded by The Associated Press').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always name the source (radio, Reuters, Algiers radio, German radio, Associated Press, official communique) and indicate if the report was recorded or relayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report opposing/foreign claims with attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting enemy or foreign-side claims, present them as claims and attribute them (e.g., 'The German communique said...', 'The Italian communique ... acknowledged that 60 dead...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print both sides' statements but clearly attribute them rather than asserting them as fact; use parentheses and qualifiers where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use qualifying language for unconfirmed or second-hand information
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualify uncertain reports with phrases such as 'was reported', 'it was announced', 'said', 'was said to have been', 'delayed', or note when broadcasts were 'recorded'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signal uncertainty and source distance to the reader; the article repeatedly uses qualifying verbs and parenthetical notes for tentative items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific geographic and numeric details with attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply precise place names, distances and numbers (e.g., 'Kairouan is 34 miles southwest of Sousse', 'Axis Force Put At 210,000', 'more than 125 miles in the six days following...') and, where needed, attribute their origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exact locations and counts to give scale and specificity, and attribute estimates to their source (military quarters, broadcasts, communiqués).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on military communiqués and official statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use official military communiqués and air force communiques as primary documentary sources (e.g., 'the war bulletin said', 'the Allied communique termed a continuation...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite official communiqués for operational claims, noting when they are recorded or relayed through other services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include correspondent eye-witness and human-interest details
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment hard reporting with on-the-ground color and human scenes—crowds cheering, local guides, mosque visits, descriptions of destroyed neighborhoods—to convey atmosphere (e.g., 'Men, women and children strewed the Army’s path with flowers', 'The fortress walls ... showed little war damage').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use first-hand observation and local voices to give readers a sense of the scene and civilian reaction alongside operational facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record delays, recording context and chain-of-transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Note when reports are delayed, recorded, or relayed through intermediaries (e.g., 'delayed', 'recorded by the Associated Press', 'broadcast recorded in London').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear the transmission history of a report (when, where, and how it was recorded or rebroadcast) to allow readers to assess timeliness and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present casualty, capture and loss figures with caution and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: When giving prisoner counts, casualties or destroyed equipment, attribute the figures (e.g., 'The score for yesterday was seven Axis planes shot down to two lost by the Allies', '20,000 prisoners in the Eighth Army’s bag').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid presenting such figures as incontrovertible fact; indicate their source (communique, military quarters, radio) and, where appropriate, describe them as estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest/submission procedural rule: deadline and award condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Compositions must be submitted before a stated deadline and the prize may be withheld if no entry is judged worthy (page fragment: 'Compositions must be submit[ted] before June 1. If none is found worthy, the government prize will not be awarded.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When announcing contests/prizes, specify submission deadlines and the condition that no award will be given if entries fail to meet standards.
